Voaters, What is your most interesting Craigslist experience?

I'm comment farming, so I'll bite. I do a fair amount of selling and buying off Craigslist, but I almost always make it a point to meet at a public place (gas station or wherever). Well, I needed a stump ground in the front of my house and there's no way that can be done remotely, so I'm calling several ads trying to find a relatively cheap guy/girl to take care of this bloody thing. Sure enough, I hit the jackpot. This guy sounds like Billy Bob Thorton from Sling Blade or whatever. Comes out in what looks like a mad max rig, towing this 1950s stump grinder and proceeds to go ape shit on the stump with this ridiculous contraption. Ridiculous, yet extremely effective. After 30 minutes of grinding, this tree stump whisperer rides off into the sunset and my yard is stump free. Cliched, but although he wasn't the hero I wanted, he was the hero I needed.
What? Where's the twist ending? Where's the loch ness monster? /s
yeah, sorry--I'm sure you were expecting more, sorry! I did preface this with I need some bloody comment points to get going on this thing.
What'd you pay him? It's craiglist, so I assume you swapped a t-shirt stained with a B-list celebrity's blood.

I gave him like 40 bucks. I bet it cost him $20 in gas to get to the house. I wish I had taken pictures of the ride AND the grinder though. Prolly not the most interesting story in the world but I swear to craigslist, I got a fookin hellava deal.
Went to buy a couch, ended up turning it down, but a friend of the seller is now my husband almost 4 years later. It's always fun telling people we met through Craigslist.
Had to do a double take on that! Nice!

We saw a posting for someone who wanted a room, but he wasn't local and was on the other side of the country.

We needed a roommate, so we messaged him.

He flew into town, checked out several rooms(with other people), wasn't weird, and provided a cash deposit on our room without needing 'just a few months to get on my feet' or whatever other excuse people there use for not paying rent.

That was kind of weird to us, how much polar-opposite he was to the typical craigslist ad/scam.

EDIT: Got scammed fake tickets. When I asked for the email receipt, he texted his 'wife' to send it to me, and they sent it in just a minute. They were fast when I thought I caught them off-guard, so that helped me think they were legit.

Also wife rented a room from someone who (after signing the lease) told them no internet, no friends over, and no kitchen before 9 am or after 8 pm.

I was selling my PS3 a few years back and met the guy at a nearby hospital parking lot. It was actually the parking lot to the ER, anyway he looked through everything I had offered with the PS3 then tried to low ball me. My personal motto with craigslist is that if I need money that bad, I am not going to ask ridiculous prices. I put stuff on craigslist all of the time and am usually one of the cheapest with said item.

Anyways, I meet the dude, he low balls me and when I deny him he jokingly says "Give me the PS3 and all of your money or I'll cut your head off" He says it in a manner where its borderline serious and joking, as if he wish he had the confidence to do it but wanted to gauge my reaction in case I took the bait. I laughed it off but felt very awkward after he took my initial offer.

I always price things 20-30% higher for this reason.

Edit: the low balling. Not the head chopping off.
And that's why I don't meet in parking lots.

I was selling a TV, and this really shady person responded. You know the drill, they are "out of the country" for the moment, wants to send a check way over the value of tv, have me mail it, etc.

So obviously I'm not selling it to this person, but I don't mind messing with them. I string them along with excuses, and feign ignorance with several things and they get REALLY mad.

At the end the scammer is trying to threaten me, and make me scared, that he is going to come to my house and hurt me, etc.

Now during this conversation, I was using my real email and I provided him my real name(also my email has my full real name in it.) But at the end he says...

"Oh and I know who you really are... Gary Coleman!"

See I have a Facebook account that I only made for Spotify, so I just used a fake name (it isn't Gary Coleman, but a similar star, but as I think I'm the only one listed as that name, and I have a few real people linked to it, I don't want to post it.)

I just thought it was hilarious this guy, who was building up with rage, to try and scare me, ends his threats with the name of a ridiculous movie star. I couldn't stop laughing.
God I've always wanted to try messing with a scammer. Every time, though, they catch on early and stop messaging me. Maybe it's a skill...
Hah, maybe they've gotten wise. People have been scambaiting since the early 2000's at this point. I bet they still have all the classics up at "419eater.com".

I sold a jeep on craigslist once, and among other calls i received, one old guys calls up and says, "well, I don't have much cash, but how many hogs would you take for that thing?"

Several lessons learned there.

I was selling my TV, I posted it with a detailed description and multiple pictures. I got a text from a potential buyer asking specific details that were explicitly in my description, I thought it was weird but she said her name and it definitely sounded like an old woman's name. I answered her questions, many of which were in the description, and she said she wanted the tv. I gave her my address to come get the tv, (it was big and I didn't want to lug it to some public place, and she seemed like a nice old lady). She shows up with her boyfriend, not old at all, both her and her boyfriend look high. they grab the tv load it into the backseat of their car (awkward as it wasn't a small tv) and leave. They didn't want to see the TV working or anything, paid with cash off a huge roll of 20s and left. I was paranoid for months afterwards.

One time a friend of mine put an ad on craigslist for a very very reasonably priced bed, but used the phone number of a person he hates. That person (also a friend of mine) received calls all through the day and night for a week, until he contacted Craigslist and had the ad removed.
Some buddies of mine listed their friends truck for cheap with his number. He got non stop calls. Haha.

Mildly interesting would be too generous, probably, but here's my most interesting craigslist experience. My car got smashed from behind earlier this year and I needed to replace it. I work nights and I'm not really much of a car guy, so my dad did this for me. He called up his buddy and headed out to check out cars. I ended up getting a vehicle from a guy a state over who was on the fire department. A few weeks later his buddy calls him up, says he's going out to meet a guy who's selling a boat. Apparently they realized about halfway there it was the same guy. They pull up and say they're looking for, let's go call him Rick, about the boat he's selling, and made some comment about having just bought a Chevy off of him. The guy turned and yelled, "Hey Rick! That guy who bought your truck is back, and he brought his friend so they can kick your ass."

And that's my only interaction with craigslist ever, so technically it's my most interesting. And it was really second hand I guess. Yep.

Went to buy a computer off CL, it was a custom built rig in an Alienware case. Really cheap for everything that came with it. We meet up, he opens up his trunk, and everything is there looking really nice. I ask if I can open up the case to look inside. He said he's never done it before and doesn't know how (Apparently someone else built it for him). I figure it out, the door is on hinges. Inside, I find (I shit you not) 2 dead hamsters that have must have been in there for at least 6 months, casually decomposing next to the PSU. Once the man sees them he muttered "oh my god" then started bawling. He explained that those were his daughter's and that they spent weeks looking for them. He ended up giving me all the stuff for free. The thing I don't understand was that this case is built like a tank. There's no way in hell a hamster would be able to get inside of it. I ended up cleaning out the inside of it, and moving everything into a new case (750D, would recommend).

So my wife was looking for a job once upon a time. She started sending her resume to jobs posted on CL. One responded and said they want to hire her.

But, it was a new twist on an old scam. They were hiring her and wanted her to start in 2 weeks. But they were overnighting a money order for $2,500 over what they wanted to pay her. She was to cash it, send the money over the amount back, then keep the rest.

She had been putting our address on her resume, so they had already sent the money order at the same time that they sent email about it. The next day we get it. It was obvious a forgery (torn, not perforated; wrong kind of paper; non-functioning watermarks), so I told them to send a prepaid envelope if they wanted it back. I also told them we would gladly cash it then hold the funds for 180 days. If it clears for that long, we'll talk about sending them the money.

We never heard back from them. We also stopped putting our home address on our resumes.

EDIT: It was interesting as I'd never seen that vector for that scam before. I'd seen it selling stuff plenty of times, but I had never thought about it be used that way. I thought it was especially shitty as they're trying to scam people who, as a lot of job seekers are unemployed, are already down on their luck.
